title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction, background defrag, and spillover paging for memory-managed KV store
author: Priya Patel
description: Context: KV cache OOMs and high eviction churn have been a recurring source of degraded throughput and tail latency for long-context workloads. This change introduces a multi-pronged memory management improvement: adaptive eviction priority, asynchronous spillover paging to host memory, and a low-latency background defragmentation/compaction thread. The goal is to reduce destructive fragmentation and unnecessary full-evictions while keeping p99 latency impact under 1% for typical conversational workloads.  Design summary: 1) Adaptive eviction priority: instead of pure recency, eviction score now combines (a) recency, (b) per-key "hotness" derived from recent access frequency and TTL, (c) estimated key size fragmentation penalty, and (d) model-variant affinity score (keys pinned for heavy-weight model variants get higher retention). We expose tuning knobs via the runtime config (kv.eviction.alpha, kv.eviction.fragmentation_weight, kv.eviction.spill_threshold).  2) Spillover paging: when GPU-resident KV memory crosses spill_threshold, we asynchronously page cold fragments to host RAM using a compact serialized representation (LZ4-compressed deltas). Paging is non-blocking: read-path checks both GPU and host pages and fetches missing entries into GPU memory on demand with a low-priority async rehydrate task. The implementation uses pinned host buffers and a batched copy to reduce PCIe overhead.  3) Background defrag/compaction: a low-priority background worker coalesces small fragments into larger contiguous blocks and updates index pointers atomically. Compaction is incremental and rate-limited (kv.compaction.max_bytes_per_sec) to avoid contention with serving. Compaction also emits metrics to track bytes reclaimed and average fragment size.  4) Heuristics and safety: eviction and compaction heuristics prefer moving long-sequence KV entries to host first and prioritize keeping short-prefix entries in GPU for latency-sensitive reuse. For models with strict latency SLOs we allow a "pin-list" of keys per model variant that are never spilled. A safety circuit triggers full-eviction only if host memory and GPU memory are both saturated.  Why this approach: previous releases used a simple LRU-like policy which caused high churn for workloads with many long contexts and interleaved short chats. Empirically, fragmentation caused up to 30% of usable KV capacity to be wasted. Combining adaptive scoring, spillover, and compaction reduces both churn and waste without changing API surface.  Implementation notes: changes are in the runtime cache engine (cpp/kv_store/*), a new host_pager component (cpp/kv_store/host_pager.{cc,h}), compaction worker (cpp/kv_store/compactor.{cc,h}), config bindings (cpp/config/kv_config.{cc,h}), and a Python integration harness for end-to-end tests (e2e/kv_spillover_test.py). We added a set of perf benches in perf/kv_bench to validate throughput and p99 under synthetic long-context workloads.  Testing and metrics: unit tests cover eviction scoring, spill serialization, and corner cases around partial rehydration. Integration tests exercise spill/rehydrate under sustained load; the e2e harness includes fault-injection to simulate host OOMs and PCIe stalls. New metrics: kv.evictions_total, kv.spill_pages, kv.rehydrate_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), kv.compaction_bytes_reclaimed, and kv.fragmentation_ratio.  Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag kv.enable_spillover (default off in main). Canary rollout for Dedicated first (5% traffic), monitor kv.rehydrate_latency_ms and request tail latency. If metrics are stable (no >2% regression in p99), expand to hosted API. We also added a graceful fallback to disable spillover per node if host paging fails more than N times.  Related work: follows ENG-4921 (spike experiment) and ENG-5032 (observability gaps). This PR consolidates previous experiments (see related PRs in the repo) and puts in hardened production-safe defaults.  Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Perf benchmarks - [x] Rollout gating and metrics - [x] Docs update (redwood-docs/kv-cache-memory.md)
commits: 5 commits: 1) initial host pager skeleton and config bindings; 2) adaptive eviction scoring algorithm + unit tests; 3) background compactor implementation and metrics; 4) spill serialization and rehydrate path with batched PCIe copy; 5) perf benches and e2e harness + docs update.
review_comments: Ethan Nguyen: Can we quantify the p99 tail impact during rehydrate under high QPS? Please add perf numbers to the PR description.
Priya Patel: Added perf bench results; worst-case p99 regressions observed were ~0.6% and average throughput unchanged within noise. See performance_summary.
Marco Alvarez: The compaction worker looks good, but I'm worried about atomic pointer updates on the hot path. Please ensure the read path uses sequence numbers to avoid ABA.
Priya Patel: Switched to sequence-numbered pointer updates and added unit tests covering concurrent readers. PTAL.
Lina Zhou: CI flaked on gpu-integration the first run (timeout). Re-ran and it passed. Approving after green CI.
performance_summary: Bench results (perf/kv_bench/long_context_bench): baseline (v1) vs this change (v2) with 128k tokens active keys across 8 models: evictions reduced by 68% (from 1.8k/min to 576/min), fragmentation_ratio reduced from 32% to 9%, OOMs observed in stress test: 0 for v2 (was 3 for baseline), p99 latency regression: +0.6% worst-case in extreme rehydrate storms (mitigated by rate limits), overall throughput change: +0.8% due to reduced eviction churn.
testing: Unit tests added for eviction score computation, spill serialization/deserialization, compactor invariants. Integration harness runs e2e/kv_spillover_test.py which simulates host paging backpressure; tests were run in CI on dedicated GPU runners and locally against a scale harness. Added fault injection test that simulates host OOM and verifies fallback to full-eviction after N retries.
rollout_plan: Feature-gated off by default. Canary flow: enable kv.enable_spillover=true on 5% of Dedicated nodes for 48h, monitor kv.rehydrate_latency_ms p99, kv.evictions_total, and node OOMs. If stable, increase to 25% for 72h, then 100% for Dedicated. Hosted API rollout will be opt-in per-customer via runtime config and require opt-in during initial pilot.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: host paging could increase tail latency for cold rehydrates. Mitigation: async low-priority rehydrate with batching, pin-list for latency-critical model variants, rate-limited compaction, and circuit breaker to disable spillover on node-level when rehydrate latency exceeds threshold. Risk: serialization bugs causing stale pointers; mitigation: sequence-numbered atomic pointer updates and unit tests that cover concurrent readers/writers.
release_notes: Added adaptive KV eviction policy, host spillover paging, and background compaction/defragmentation to reduce KV memory fragmentation and evictions. Feature is off by default and controlled via kv.enable_spillover. See docs/kv-cache-memory.md for tuning and observability. Impact: lower OOM rate and reduced eviction churn for long-context workloads.
